extraAngles.prompt: THE PEER-REVIEWED STUDIES THE FIRST SWEEP MISSED, read at the primary (arXiv HTML or the ACM/ACL PDF): Mirowski et al., 'A Robot Walks into a Bar' (FAccT 2024, arXiv 2405.20956; humour); Subbiah et al., 'Reading Subtext' (TACL 2024, arXiv 2403.01061); Ippolito et al. 2022 (arXiv 2211.05030) and Chakrabarty et al. 2023 'Creativity Support in the Age of LLMs' (arXiv 2309.12570); Agarwal, Naaman and Vashistha (CHI 2025, arXiv 2409.11360) and Moon, Green and Kushlev 2024 on cultural homogenisation; Köbis and Mossink 2021 (CHB 114:106553), Walsh, Preus and Gronski 2024 and Walsh, Preus and Antoniak 2024 on verse; Weber-Wulff et al. 2023 (IJEI 19:26), Dugan et al. 2023 (AAAI), Ippolito et al. 2020 (ACL) on detection and the neurodivergent-writer false positives; Bender and Koller 2020 and Bender et al. 2021 — extract the concrete failure modes each measures and the register it measured them in

STEERABILITY and MECHANISM — the case against the first sweep's claim that no prompt, temperature or model switch fixes the tells: Kirk et al. ICLR 2024 (RLHF reduces diversity), Zhang et al. 2025 'Verbalized Sampling' (arXiv 2510.01171), Lanchantin et al. 2025, Sharma et al. 2023 'Towards Understanding Sycophancy' (arXiv 2310.13548), Shumailov et al. 2024 (Nature, model collapse) as the sameness mechanism — read each primary and say what it shows about whether the failure modes are fixed traits, training artefacts, or prompt-movable

GAMES RESEARCH and PRACTICE beyond trade press: CALYPSO (AIIDE 2023), Max Kreminski's papers on LLM story generation, Emily Short on LLM NPCs and narrative, Ubisoft's Neo NPC at GDC 2024, Square Enix's Portopia (April 2023) reception, AI Dungeon, Keywords Studios' abandoned all-AI game (2024), Xalavier Nelson Jr.; and the reviewers who have read AI-written adventure modules — tenfootpole.org, The Alexandrian, Sly Flourish — what each says fails in generated GAME prose and read-aloud

THE COUNTER-CASE that generated fiction can be good, and the publishing primaries: Jeanette Winterson's Guardian defence of the OpenAI metafiction story (March 2025); Rie Kudan's Akutagawa Prize novel (January 2024); Mark Lawrence's 2023 blind reader test; Vauhini Vara's 'Ghosts' (2021); Sudowrite's Muse claims as the vendor pole; Jane Friedman (August 2023); the Authors Guild 2023 survey; OneBookShelf's own policy text; Clarkesworld 'A Concerning Trend' (15 Feb 2023) and NPR's 2023 Clarke interview; Alex Hern's Guardian TechScape (May 2024) on the 'delve' dialect dispute — read the primaries, not the paraphrases

CRITICS DIRECT, at the primary: Ted Chiang's New Yorker essay (31 Aug 2024) — the most-cited critic, so far seen only secondhand; Neil Clarke's own blog; Laura Preston's n+1 essay; Charlie Guo; Mohammad Siam; Ethan Mollick; Elizabeth Goodspeed; Nostalgebraist; Mark Williams / TNPS; Weixin Liang's self-edit study; plus Robin Sloan, John Scalzi, Chuck Wendig, Cory Doctorow, Tiffany Yates Martin, Victoria Strauss — what each says generated prose gets wrong in FICTION and what a human editor sees first
